Class CobolSql

java.lang.Object
org.cobol4j.CobolSql
public final class CobolSql extends Object
COBOL embedded SQL semantics over JDBC.

Wraps a JDBC Connection with COBOL-style SQL operations: host variable binding from Record fields, SQLCA state management, cursor lifecycle, and fluent builders for all SQL verbs.

SELECT INTO (single row): 

sql.select("SELECT NAME, BALANCE FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE ID = ?")
   .param(rec, "WS-CUST-ID")
   .into(rec, "WS-NAME", "WS-BALANCE")
   .execute();

if (sql.isNotFound()) {
    // handle missing customer
}
CURSOR (multi-row): 
SqlCursor cursor = sql.declareCursor("CUST-CURSOR",
    "SELECT NAME, BALANCE FROM CUSTOMERS ORDER BY NAME");

sql.open(cursor);
sql.fetch(cursor).into(rec, "WS-NAME", "WS-BALANCE").execute();
while (sql.isSuccess()) {
    // process row
    sql.fetch(cursor).into(rec, "WS-NAME", "WS-BALANCE").execute();
}
sql.close(cursor);
DML (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE): 
sql.execute("INSERT INTO CUSTOMERS (ID, NAME, BALANCE) VALUES (?, ?, ?)")
   .params(rec, "WS-ID", "WS-NAME", "WS-BALANCE")
   .execute();

      public CobolSql.SelectBuilder select(String sql)
      Begin a SELECT statement that returns at most one row. The SQL should NOT include an INTO clause — use the fluent CobolSql.SelectBuilder.into(Record, String...) method instead.
